findings: Both captures describe UPI on Link for eligible onboarded US businesses subject to restricted-business exclusions, INR presentment, one-time on-session payments and only Payment Links, hosted Stripe Checkout and Elements. Turning on Link auto-enables UPI subject to eligibility, without per-method integration changes; November retains these constraints (old 7-25; new 8-13, 27-38). Interest-form submission (new 15-25) does not make access active or establish other countries or a global preview status.

November changes the documented floor from 1 INR to 0.50 USD equivalent in INR; 100,000 INR maximum remains. Existing source line 17, Stripe index line 446 and Link concept lines 54 and 174 still give the May floor. Add a dated route qualifier and preserve old provenance (old 20-25; new 33-38).

Both captures preserve new and returning buyer flow. Desktop QR and mobile app selection/redirect route to the banking/wallet authentication and approval step. A new buyer supplies information and is signed up to Link after transaction completion; returning Link users have saved name, address and virtual payment address. Storage and return/notification do not by themselves establish payment or merchant settlement (old 27-47; new 40-60).

Refund and dispute text is semantically unchanged (old 49-55; new 62-68). Source lines 24-31 correctly preserve timing, events and failure recovery but should name the final `Refund` states and attach merchant debit explicitly to an accepted bank/PSP dispute request. No payout or settlement-currency guarantee in these UPI-on-Link captures.
Root index line 7 leads to Stripe index lines 441-446 and 736, then Link concept lines 34-54 and 169-174. Keep the generic Link properties distinct from funding-method-specific limits.
substantive_changes: The November Link-specific floor is 0.50 USD equivalent in INR, replacing May's 1 INR. Both keep the INR 100,000 maximum and INR presentment (new 33-38 versus old 20-25).

November adds an email interest/access request route (new 15-25), while the US availability banner and eligible US business language remain. The request is not activation and does not by itself say UPI on Link is universally private-preview-only.
historical_claims_to_preserve: May's 1 INR floor remains dated. Link auto-enable is always qualified by seller onboarding, restrictions, method eligibility and named UI scope. Preserve neither global Link access nor guaranteed session display from the auto-enable wording (old 14-25; new 27-38).

May and November preserve one-time on-session, bank/wallet authentication, and the new/returning Link distinction (old 7-25, 27-47; new 8-13, 27-60). Stored personal details do not constitute recurring authorization.

Both capture up to 60 days after original payment for refund requests. Up to seven business days is processing time, while `refund.updated` or `refund.failed` give final state. On `succeeded` refund is successful; `failed` returns funds to Stripe balance and calls for an alternate refund. Bank/PSP dispute acceptance drives immediate non-contestable Stripe debit (old 49-55; new 62-68).
conflicts: Do not borrow direct UPI's 1 INR November floor or UPI AutoPay e-mandate/15,000 INR recurring limit. Direct UPI note (raw/stripe-payments-upi-2026-11-07.md:8-25, 122-124) and UPI on Link new 27-38 are different routes with different eligibility and authorization models. Link concept line 39's generic recurring label cannot override Link UPI one-time/on-session scope.

Keep seller location and buyer context distinct. General Link May business-locations carveout for India (raw/stripe-link-2025.md:54-59) and November country availability note (raw/stripe-payments-link-2026-11-07.md:15-17) do not disqualify eligible US sellers serving UPI customers or establish India-based merchant access. INR presentment does not by itself establish merchant settlement currency. General Link overview lines 8-11 describe Stripe balance settlement on a card timeline for successful payments but are not an external payout guarantee or funding-specific refund rule.

The Link methods companion places UPI and Pix in group `lfsg_002` and says position of funding group is integration dependent in Charge data. Group is shared and does not by itself identify UPI; dashboard Link versus card-brand Link representation is not the underlying UPI method identity. Auto-enablement does not entail per-session display (raw/stripe-payments-link-link-payment-methods-2026-11-07.md:11-23, 27-50).
unresolved_questions: The request-interest form does not establish availability outside eligible US sellers, an access decision, or any specific merchant's activation, display, settlement currency or payout.

findings: Keep both dated captures. Correct the minimum to 0.50 USD equivalent in INR for November while preserving May's 1 INR, keep 100,000 INR upper bound, qualify auto-enable, add request/access distinction and maintain first-time/saved details and asynchronous refund outcome.
conflicts: Update reciprocal Link concept/index lines with dated floors. Distinguish eligible US sellers and INR/Indian-rail buyer scope from general Link's India account carveout. Explicitly distinguish one-time on-session UPI on Link from direct UPI, AutoPay and generic Link recurring or refund properties.
source_assessments.reason: The November floor materially differs and the May-only source and routes would produce an incorrect minimum; secondary eligibility, refund and payment outcomes can also be made more exact.

answers.Q1: The November 7, 2026 capture at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/upi describes UPI on Link for eligible onboarded US businesses outside restricted categories, for one-time, on-session payments presented in INR. Turn on Link for automatic UPI enablement subject to eligibility, on Payment Links, hosted Checkout or Elements. November changes the minimum to 0.50 USD equivalent in INR, keeps the INR 100,000 maximum, and adds an email request route that does not establish granted access (new raw lines 15-38 and old raw lines 14-25). Desktop uses a QR; mobile lists UPI apps and redirects to the selected app. Banking or wallet app authorization is required. The illustrated new buyer supplies information and signs up once the transaction completes; returning buyers have saved name, address and virtual payment address. Return or notification alone does not establish merchant settlement (new raw lines 40-60 and old raw lines 27-47). Refund requests are allowed up to 60 days and complete asynchronously, up to seven business days. `refund.updated` or `refund.failed` report final `Refund` status. `succeeded` and `failed` differ; failure returns the amount to the Stripe balance and requires another refund method. If the customer's bank or PSP accepts their request to return funds, the merchant cannot contest and Stripe immediately removes funds (new raw lines 62-68 and old raw lines 49-55). source-stripe-upi-on-link.md preserves the main flow but its 1 INR minimum is May-specific.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/upi, the substantive changes are the documented floor from May's 1 INR to November's 0.50 USD equivalent in INR, and the new access-interest form. The 100,000 INR maximum, eligible US merchant scope, one-time on-session INR use and only three UI routes persist (old raw lines 14-25 and new raw lines 15-38). Rewording and numbering the customer steps and changing refund webhook formatting are presentational. Preserve the dated approved scope, saved details, 60-day submission and seven-business-day asynchronous completion, final Refund states and conditional bank/PSP dispute debit in source-stripe-upi-on-link.md (old raw lines 27-55 and new raw lines 40-68). Update the reciprocal Link concept/index floor and distinguish the separate direct UPI 1 INR limit and AutoPay mandate from UPI on Link. An eligible US seller can offer UPI in INR even though the general Link availability caveat excludes India-based Stripe accounts. The interest form, QR, return and refund submission do not themselves establish access, verified payment success, buyer bank credit or payout. INR is the presentment currency in the guide, without a separate merchant settlement currency or payout commitment.
